subject: Inference stability checklist & kernel audit — MAP deliverable
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@heliosanalytics.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference stability checklist & kernel audit — MAP deliverable

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the kickoff earlier — the Helios model ops team asked me to capture a few clarifying points before we lock the MAP:

- Our priority is TTFT (time-to-first-token) under a 512-token prompt for the customer-facing QA flow. Target = <= 120ms median.
- Concurrency: we want to validate sustained 50 concurrent requests without P90 latency regression.
- Quant paths: we need head-to-head FP16/BF16 vs INT8 and an exploratory INT4 profile. For INT paths, we need accuracy regressions measured on our 1,200-sample QA set.

Can you confirm the exact artifacts you will hand over (raw logs, kernel profiles, CSV of per-request traces)? Also, procurement wants any throughput numbers in the MAP so they can sign the SOW.

Appreciate it,
Jordan

Jordan Park
Director, ML Systems
Helios Analytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference stability checklist & kernel audit — MAP deliverable

Jordan —

Thanks, that aligns with our understanding. Below is the MAP deliverable breakdown we'll include in v1.3 (attached). Summary + acceptance criteria:

1) Latency (TTFT) + throughput artifacts
   - Deliverable: CSV of per-request TTFT and per-token latencies for each model/quant path.
   - Acceptance: Median TTFT <= 120ms on customer baseline; P95 <= 250ms under 50 concurrent sustained QPS.

2) Concurrency stress test
   - Deliverable: JMeter/Locust scripts, cluster config, and aggregated traces.
   - Acceptance: No timeouts or model crashes across a 30-minute sustained 50-concurrent workload; tail latency (P99) increase <= 2x baseline.

3) Quant + kernel profiles
   - Deliverable: Kernel flamegraphs (PDF), per-op INT8/INT4 drop-in regressions, and a short kernel compatibility note.
   - Acceptance: Token-generation quality (Helios QA set) regression <= 1.5% relative to FP16 median BLEU-like score; otherwise we mark INT path as experimental.

4) Regression checks and rollbacks
   - Deliverable: Automated regression run (scripts + diff report), recommended fallback policy in MAP (FP16 auto-fallback).
   - Acceptance: Any regression > 2.0% triggers canary rollback and a joint action item.

Attachments included: MAP_v1.3.docx (deliverables + timeline). We will run the initial benchmarks using your model snapshot 20270601-v3 on a p4d-like Dedicated pool and share raw traces + the summarized CSV by EOD Thursday.

Next steps:
- Marcus will schedule the concurrency run (Wed AM). Priyom will run the INT8/INT4 quant profiles (Wed afternoon).
- Jordan: please confirm the Helios QA set location (Drive link) or send samples if there are any pre-processing steps we should apply.

Thanks — I’ll loop back with CSVs and kernel profiles once runs complete.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Olga / team — quick status:

- Concurrency run started 2027-06-16T08:00Z against model 20270601-v3 on Dedicated pool (8x A100). Load profile: warmup 5m, ramp to 50 concurrent over 3m, sustain 30m.
- Observations so far (first 12 minutes aggregated): median TTFT = 112ms (FP16); P95 = 238ms; P99 = 480ms (spiky, investigating hot-AI-worker behavior).
- INT8 run queued now (Priyom). We'll collect KV cache metrics separately; initial memory pressure looks within expected range.

Jordan — attaching a short raw CSV (helios_map_ttft_results.csv) and an early kernel summary (kernel_profile_report.pdf). Note the INT8 path may require a custom kernel patch for fused attention to hit similar latency.

Attaching: helios_map_ttft_results.csv (csv), kernel_profile_report.pdf (pdf)

Marcus
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@heliosanalytics.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference stability checklist & kernel audit — MAP deliverable

Jordan / Olga —

Final notes from the quant/kernel audit and recommended MAP updates (attached full PDF):

- FP16 vs BF16: BF16 ran within noise of FP16 across TTFT/throughput; choose BF16 only if downstream training consistency is required.
- INT8: Per-token throughput improved ~1.6x median, median TTFT = 70ms, but on the Helios QA set we saw an average quality drop of 1.9% (relative). That sits under our 2.0% alert but above the conservative 1.5% acceptance in the MAP — recommend INT8 as "canary for non-critical flows" and FP16 auto-fallback for critical customer-facing endpoints.
- INT4 exploratory: 2.8x token throughput vs FP16 but quality regression > 6%; not recommended for production.
- Kernel issues: Two kernels required minor adjustment (fused softmax path and KV packing) for INT8 to avoid tail latencies. Patch proposals included in kernel_profile_report.pdf.
- Regression checks: We ran 3 repeats; variance was low (stddev < 3% on median TTFT). Attached CSV includes per-trial breakdown and a small script (run_regressions.sh) we used.

Action items for MAP update:
- Mark INT8 as "experimental but supported with fallback" in Section 3.2.
- Add a 2-week canary in prod for INT8 traffic capped at 5% of requests with continuous eval.
- Include kernel patch PRs as part of deployment checklist.

Jordan: please let us know if procurement needs the summarized throughput numbers in a specific format for the SOW. We can produce a one-page SLO table for procurement review.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior ML Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: kernel_profile_report.pdf (pdf), helios_map_ttft_results.csv (csv)
